Established on [[March 31, 1874]], as the [[Military Horse Bureau]] (軍馬局), the agency went through several reorganizations, including the Military Horse Breeding Station (軍馬育成所) and Military Horse Supplementary Station (軍馬補充署). It was officially renamed as the Military Horse Supplementary Department under the "Military Horse Supplementary Department Ordinance" on [[May 9, 1896]]. The department operated with a headquarters led by a chief and maintained multiple branches across Japan. It was dissolved along with the Ministry of the Army in [[:en:November 1945|November 1945]].
== History====
=== Establishment and Early Development==== The Military Horse Bureau, formed on March 31, 1874, under the "Military Horse Bureau Ordinance," managed horse policy and conducted military horse training. It supervised Tokyo's First Stable and Sendai's Second Stable. The 1884 ordinance expanded its responsibilities to include the purchase and breeding of foals, leading to the establishment of the First Horse Training Corps (Tokyo), Second Horse Training Corps (Miyagi), and the Sanbongi branch station.
In 1886, the bureau was dissolved, and its duties were transferred to the Cavalry Bureau's third division. By 1888, the Military Horse Breeding Station was established under the Cavalry Bureau, incorporating the former training corps as its branches in Aomori, Kajiya Sawa, and Aono Plain.
=== Transition to Supplementary Department==== The Military Horse Breeding Station was reorganized into the Military Horse Supplementary Station on May 3, 1896, becoming a directly controlled agency of the [[Minister of the Army]]. Shortly afterward, it was renamed the Military Horse Supplementary Department on May 9, 1896, with branch offices established in Sanbongi, Kajiya Sawa, Fukumoto, and Aono.<ref name="shibu">"Establishment of Military Horse Supplementary Department Branches"</ref> By 1897, a new branch was set up in Shirakawa, and in 1899, the headquarters moved to Ichigaya in Tokyo.
In the early 20th century, additional branches were established, including Kushiro (1900) in Hokkaido, Kawakami (1908), and Tokachi (1909). The department continued expanding its facilities and operations to support Japan's military horse needs, including managing regional offices, training facilities, and supporting infrastructure.
=== Final Years and Dissolution==== In 1944, the branch offices were renamed "Central Horse Depots" in response to wartime restructuring. The department was ultimately dissolved in November 1945, following the abolition of the Ministry of the Army after [[:en:Pacific War|Pacific War]].
== Leadership==== The department was led by a chief, often a high-Ranking cavalry officer. Below is a partial list of notable chiefs: * Col. [[Heizo Okura]] (May 11, 1896 – October 16, 1896, concurrent post as Chief of Horse Policy Division) * Gen. [[Takemoto Hikojiro]] (1911–1913) * Lt. Gen. [[Tadashi Ueda]] (1926–1929) * Maj. Gen. [[Seiji Wada]] (1939–1941)
== Branches and Operations====
=== Sanbongi Branch==== Located in [[Sanbongi]], Aomori Prefecture, this branch was one of the largest facilities, managing multiple sub-stations and pastures. The administrative building later became part of the [[Towada City Local Museum]].
=== Kushiro Branch==== Established in Hokkaido's [[Shiranuka District]], the branch focused on horse breeding and training. Post-war, the site was repurposed for forestry management.
=== Shirakawa Branch==== Located in [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]], this branch operated multiple facilities, including pastures and sub-stations. The administrative building now houses the Nishigo Village History and Folk Museum.
=== Other Branches==== * '''Kawakami Branch:''' Established in Hokkaido's [[:en:Shibecha|Shibecha]], this branch utilized land from a former penal colony. * '''Tokachi Branch:''' Located in [[:en:Tokachi Subprefecture|Tokachi Subprefecture]], this branch was instrumental in training military horses. * '''Aono Branch:''' Situated in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]], it served as a breeding and training center.
== Legacy==== Many of the department's facilities were repurposed after the war for agricultural, educational, and forestry uses. For example: - The Shirakawa Branch became part of [[:en:Tohoku University|Tohoku University]]'s research facilities. - The Towada City Local Museum preserves historical artifacts and documents from the Sanbongi Branch. - Former buildings in Kushiro and Kawakami were repurposed as local administrative offices.
== Related Articles==== * [[:en:Imperial Japanese Army|Imperial Japanese Army]] * [[Army Veterinary School]] * [[Military Horse Epidemic Prevention Department]] * [[Japanese Ministry of the Army]]
== References==== {{Reflist}}
== Further Reading==== * Toyama, Misao, et al., "Imperial Army Organizational Overview," Vol. 1, Fuyo Shobo Publishing, 1993. ISBN 4-8295-0125-1 * Iida, Norio, "Illustrated History of Japan's Military Sites," Kawade Shobo Shinsha, 2004. ISBN 4-309-76048-1 * "The Personnel Directory of Active Army Officers," National Diet Library Digital Collection.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:軍馬補充部]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:軍馬補充部]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:軍馬補充部]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11637468]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:20, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:10, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Military Horse Supplementary Department''' (軍馬補充部, Gunba Hojubu) was a subordinate agency of the Japanese {{ill|Ministry of the Army|en|Ministry of the Army|WD=Q6017522|lt=Ministry of the Army}} tasked with the procurement, breeding, and training of military horses, as well as the management of equine resources. Established on [[March 31, 1874]], as the [[Military Horse Bureau]] (軍馬局), the agency went through several reorganizations, including the Military Horse Breeding Station (軍馬育成所) and Military Horse Supplementary Station (軍馬補充署). It was officially renamed as the Military Horse Supplementary Department under the "Military Horse Supplementary Department Ordinance" on [[May 9, 1896]]. The department operated with a headquarters led by a chief and maintained multiple branches across Japan. It was dissolved along with the Ministry of the Army in {{ill|November 1945|en|November 1945|WD=Q16667167|lt=November 1945}}.
== History====
=== Establishment and Early Development==== The Military Horse Bureau, formed on March 31, 1874, under the "Military Horse Bureau Ordinance," managed horse policy and conducted military horse training. It supervised Tokyo's First Stable and Sendai's Second Stable. The 1884 ordinance expanded its responsibilities to include the purchase and breeding of foals, leading to the establishment of the First Horse Training Corps (Tokyo), Second Horse Training Corps (Miyagi), and the Sanbongi branch station.
In 1886, the bureau was dissolved, and its duties were transferred to the Cavalry Bureau's third division. By 1888, the Military Horse Breeding Station was established under the Cavalry Bureau, incorporating the former training corps as its branches in Aomori, Kajiya Sawa, and Aono Plain.
=== Transition to Supplementary Department==== The Military Horse Breeding Station was reorganized into the Military Horse Supplementary Station on May 3, 1896, becoming a directly controlled agency of the [[Minister of the Army]]. Shortly afterward, it was renamed the Military Horse Supplementary Department on May 9, 1896, with branch offices established in Sanbongi, Kajiya Sawa, Fukumoto, and Aono.<ref name="shibu">"Establishment of Military Horse Supplementary Department Branches"</ref> By 1897, a new branch was set up in Shirakawa, and in 1899, the headquarters moved to Ichigaya in Tokyo.
In the early 20th century, additional branches were established, including Kushiro (1900) in Hokkaido, Kawakami (1908), and Tokachi (1909). The department continued expanding its facilities and operations to support Japan's military horse needs, including managing regional offices, training facilities, and supporting infrastructure.
=== Final Years and Dissolution==== In 1944, the branch offices were renamed "Central Horse Depots" in response to wartime restructuring. The department was ultimately dissolved in November 1945, following the abolition of the Ministry of the Army after {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}.
== Leadership==== The department was led by a chief, often a high-Ranking cavalry officer. Below is a partial list of notable chiefs: * Col. [[Heizo Okura]] (May 11, 1896 – October 16, 1896, concurrent post as Chief of Horse Policy Division) * Gen. [[Takemoto Hikojiro]] (1911–1913) * Lt. Gen. [[Tadashi Ueda]] (1926–1929) * Maj. Gen. [[Seiji Wada]] (1939–1941)
== Branches and Operations====
=== Sanbongi Branch==== Located in [[Sanbongi]], Aomori Prefecture, this branch was one of the largest facilities, managing multiple sub-stations and pastures. The administrative building later became part of the [[Towada City Local Museum]].

=== Shirakawa Branch==== Located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|en|Fukushima Prefecture|WD=Q71707|lt=Fukushima Prefecture}}, this branch operated multiple facilities, including pastures and sub-stations. The administrative building now houses the Nishigo Village History and Folk Museum.
=== Other Branches==== * '''Kawakami Branch:''' Established in Hokkaido's [[:en:Shibecha|Shibecha]], this branch utilized land from a former penal colony. * '''Tokachi Branch:''' Located in {{ill|Tokachi Subprefecture|en|Tokachi Subprefecture|WD=Q1137454|lt=Tokachi Subprefecture}}, this branch was instrumental in training military horses. * '''Aono Branch:''' Situated in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|WD=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}, it served as a breeding and training center.
== Legacy==== Many of the department's facilities were repurposed after the war for agricultural, educational, and forestry uses. For example: - The Shirakawa Branch became part of {{ill|Tohoku University|en|Tohoku University|WD=Q1062129|lt=Tohoku University}}'s research facilities. - The Towada City Local Museum preserves historical artifacts and documents from the Sanbongi Branch. - Former buildings in Kushiro and Kawakami were repurposed as local administrative offices.

=== Establishment and Early Development==== The Military Horse Bureau, formed on March 31, 1874, under the "Military Horse Bureau Ordinance," managed horse policy and conducted military horse training. It supervised Tokyo's First Stable and Sendai's Second Stable. The 1884 ordinance expanded its responsibilities to include the purchase and breeding of foals, leading to the establishment of the First Horse Training Corps (Tokyo), Second Horse Training Corps (Miyagi), and the Sanbongi branch station.
In 1886, the bureau was dissolved, and its duties were transferred to the Cavalry Bureau's third division. By 1888, the Military Horse Breeding Station was established under the Cavalry Bureau, incorporating the former training corps as its branches in Aomori, Kajiya Sawa, and Aono Plain.

In the early 20th century, additional branches were established, including Kushiro (1900) in Hokkaido, Kawakami (1908), and Tokachi (1909). The department continued expanding its facilities and operations to support Japan's military horse needs, including managing regional offices, training facilities, and supporting infrastructure.

[[Heizo Okura]] (May 11, 1896 – October 16, 1896, concurrent post as Chief of Horse Policy Division) * Gen. [[Takemoto Hikojiro]] (1911–1913) * Lt. Gen. [[Tadashi Ueda]] (1926–1929) * Maj. Gen. [[Seiji Wada]] (1939–1941)

=== Kushiro Branch==== Established in Hokkaido's [[Shiranuka District]], the branch focused on horse breeding and training. Post-war, the site was repurposed for forestry management.
=== Shirakawa Branch==== Located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|en|Fukushima Prefecture|WD=Q71707|lt=Fukushima Prefecture|1=Fukushima Prefecture}}, this branch operated multiple facilities, including pastures and sub-stations.
